title: Host backend: the BSP's public API built against host models, so application logic can be tested without an RP2040 image

backend_commit.note: The host backend lives entirely in picocalc_emu under bsp/host and does not use the emulator. The commit is recorded because the framebuffer digest is defined to match that backend's, and the keyboard depth bound was taken from it.

why.gap: Line clearing and collision detection are pure functions, but reaching them meant building an RP2040 image and running the emulator.
why.evidence_the_gap_was_real: docs/DOGFOODING_20260805.md gap 3. This was the last of the four the dogfooding run found.
why.revised_judgement: Milestone 2 had been assessed as lower priority once the firmware backend ran. Writing an application showed a second use for it that had not been considered: testing application logic, not merely iterating faster.

implementation.separate_from_device_build: bsp/CMakeLists.txt is untouched. The host build is a second consumer of the same public API, not a change to it.

modelled.display: A 320x320 framebuffer. The window / write_pixels semantics are kept exactly, including the write pointer wrapping within the window, because applications depend on that shape.
modelled.keyboard: A queue bounded at 31 events, with overflow counted.
modelled.psram: 8 MiB of host memory with the device's bounds behaviour. info().id reports the identity the real chip returned during hardware correlation, not a placeholder.
modelled.sdcard: An array of sectors, arriving formatted.
modelled.pico_sdk: stdio_init_all and sleep_ms only — the two symbols every application in this repository actually uses.

shared_with_the_device_build.why_this_matters: Those two BSP sources have no Pico SDK dependency at all — they speak only to picocalc::sdcard and to ChanFatFS. The host build therefore compiles the very same files the device does, on top of a RAM block device, so a host filesystem test exercises the shipping code rather than a stand-in for it.

implementation.why_the_card_arrives_formatted: The BSP mounts and never formats, and this build cannot format either: ChanFatFS is configured with FF_USE_MKFS 0, and that configuration is part of the hardware-verified device build. Changing it to make the host convenient would change what ships. So the same textbook FAT16 the emulator's card model lays down is written directly — a layout already known to mount.
implementation.narrow_sdk_shim_is_deliberate: Code that uses an unmodelled part of the chip fails to compile. That is the correct answer; a broad shim would grant false confidence from a host run.

cross_backend_property.what: framebuffer_sha256() uses the same canonical form as the firmware backend: row-major, little-endian RGB565 raw bytes.
cross_backend_property.consequence: An application that draws the same picture under both backends produces the same 64 hex characters here and in picocalc-run's framebuffer.rgb565_sha256, so the two runs can be compared directly.
cross_backend_property.why_not_hash_a_png: An encoder-settings change would move the bytes without the picture changing.

result.completion_condition: A dedicated application starts on the PC and produces screen, key and file results deterministically.

determinism.how: Checked from the outside by tools/picocalc.py test --mode host, because nothing inside the program may read a wall clock, a random source, or an address.

notable_checks: The BSP's own filesystem smoke sequence — mount, write, sync, read, compare, remove — completes, running the same sources the device builds.
The keyboard stops at 31 events and counts the 169 it discarded, reproducing the hardware constraint rather than a host artefact.
sleep_ms advances virtual time by exactly 250000 us without blocking.

defect_found.symptom: The first host run of the BSP's own smoke test failed at the write stage with no sectors ever reaching the block layer.
defect_found.cause: fatfs_diskio.cpp gates writes behind PICOCALC_BSP_ENABLE_SD_WRITE and answers RES_WRPRT without it. The device build defines it; the host build did not.
defect_found.fix: The host build defines it too, and verify_environment now checks that it still does — a silently read-only card is the kind of difference that would make host results quietly stop meaning what they appear to.

known_limitations: Directory-backed Fast SD mode, listed under Milestone 2, is not implemented. The card is an array of sectors in host memory; there is no path that shows a host directory to the application.
No multicore, no interrupts, no DMA, no PIO. Behaviour depending on any of them is invisible here and belongs to the firmware backend.
The LCD wire format does not exist on the host, so verify_pixels always reports transport_ok. It can confirm what the application computed, never that the picture reached a panel.
audio underrun_count is always zero. That is the absence of a claim, not a claim of no underruns: nothing on the host consumes samples on a schedule.
The scenario runner is firmware-backend only. Host tests are written in C++.
authority: The firmware backend remains the authority on hardware behaviour. The host backend answers whether the application computed the right thing, in under a second; it cannot see the questions the firmware backend exists to answer.
